The first larval instar feeds actively on detritus and fungal hyphae, growing steadily until the allometric shift associated with post-larval transformation. The onset of exogenous feeding begins within hours of hatching, and the actively growing larva accumulates mass quickly during this pre-metamorphic interval, preparing for the juvenile stage that follows the transformation into a functional post-metamorphic individual.

Field-collected specimens from deciduous forest litter in central Europe confirm that these laboratory-derived size maxima correspond well with the largest individuals encountered in natural populations under optimal moisture conditions, although some seasonal variation in ultimate size has been noted in response to food quality gradients.
